facts.statement: Stenopelix is a genus of basal ceratopsian that lived approximately 140 million years ago in Germany.
facts.quote: Stenopelix (meaning "narrow pelvis") is a genus of basal ceratopsian from the Early Cretaceous (late Berriasian stage, approximately 140 million years ago) of Germany.

facts.statement: The classification of Stenopelix relies on hip characteristics because the known fossil lacks a skull.
facts.quote: The genus is based on a partial skeleton lacking the skull, and its classification is based on characteristics of the hips.

facts.statement: A fossil of Stenopelix was discovered in 1855 in a sandstone quarry near Bückeburg, Germany.
facts.quote: In 1855, in a sandstone quarry near Bückeburg on the Harrl, a fossil was found of a small dinosaur.

facts.statement: Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer named the species Stenopelix valdensis in 1857.
facts.quote: In 1857, based on this fossil, Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer named the type species Stenopelix valdensis.

facts.statement: The genus name Stenopelix means "narrow pelvis" derived from Greek words.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek stenos, "narrow", and pelyx, "pelvis".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of hollow impressions of an almost complete skeleton that lacks the skull and neck.
facts.quote: The holotype, GZG 741/2 (earlier GPI 741–1, 2), found in the Obernkirchen Sandstein Formation, consists of the impressions of an almost complete skeleton, lacking the skull and the neck.

facts.statement: The fossil consists of two non-overlapping plates with hollow impressions that have been used to create gypsum and latex casts for study.
facts.quote: The two plates do not overlap completely. The hollows, serving as a natural mold, have since been used to produce several casts in gypsum and latex to facilitate the study of the specimen.

facts.statement: Stenopelix was a small herbivore reaching 1.4 meters in length and weighing 10 kilograms.
facts.quote: Stenopelix was a small herbivorous animal, reaching 1.4 m in length and 10 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: The ilium shaft tapers to a rounded point, and the ischium shaft is thickest in the middle with a distinctive kink.
facts.quote: The shaft part of the ilium uniformly tapers ending in a rounded point. The shaft of the ischium is thickest in the middle and there shows a distinctive kink.

facts.statement: Stenopelix valdensis was the only known species of the extinct genus, an ornithischian dinosaur that lived about 140 million years ago during the Berriasian stage in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Stenopelix valdensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Stenopelix (gr. "pelvis estrecha") de dinosaurio ornitisquio que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 140 millones de años, en el Berriasiense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: Stenopelix was a bipedal herbivore measuring approximately 1.5 meters in length and 0.7 meters in height.
facts.quote: Medía aproximadamente 1,5 metro de largo y 0,7 de alto. Era un herbívoro bípedo del que solo se conoce parte de la pelvis y miembros posteriores.

facts.statement: The classification of Stenopelix is controversial and problematic due to the lack of a skull.
facts.quote: La clasificación de Stenopelix es controvertida y siempre ha sido problemática debido a la falta de cráneo.

facts.statement: In 1974, Teresa Maryańska suggested Stenopelix was a pachycephalosaurian, one of the oldest known, based on the apparent exclusion of the pubis from the acetabulum and strong caudal ribs.
facts.quote: En 1974 , Teresa Maryańska sugirió que se trataba de un paquicefalosauriano, uno de los más antiguos que se conocen, debido a la aparente exclusión del pubis del acetábulo y la presencia de fuertes costillas caudales.

facts.statement: In 1982, Peter Galton demonstrated that the so-called pubis was actually part of the acetabulum and the caudal ribs were sacral ribs.
facts.quote: Peter Galton en 1982 demostró que el "pubis" era en realidad parte del acetábulo, y las llamadas "costillas caudales" eran costillas sacras .

facts.statement: Peter Galton concluded that Stenopelix was a ceratopsian.
facts.quote: Galton concluyó que Stenopelix era ceratopsiano.

facts.statement: Later cladistic analyses by Paul Sereno placed Stenopelix within Pachycephalosauria.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los análisis cladísticos posteriores realizados por Paul Sereno han dado como resultado una posición en Pachycephalosauria.

facts.statement: Paleontologists Richard J. Butler and Robert M. Sullivan view Stenopelix as Marginocephalia of uncertain position, rejecting its supposed synapomorphies with Pachycephalosauria as incorrect identifications.
facts.quote: Pero los paleontólogos Richard J. Butler y Robert M. Sullivan , no obstante, ven a la especie como Marginocephalia de posición incierta, rechazando las supuestas sinapomorfias con Pachycephalosauria como identificaciones incorrectas o carentes de contundencia debido a una posible presencia en grupos ceratópsidos.

facts.statement: A 2011 cladistic analysis by Butler et al. showed Stenopelix is a basal member of Ceratopsia with Yinlong as its sister taxon.
facts.quote: En 2011, un análisis cladístico realizado por Butler et al. mostró que Stenopelix es un miembro basal de la Ceratopsia, y su taxón hermano es Yinlong.

facts.statement: Stenopelix is classified as a member of the family Chaoyangsauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Chaoyangsauridae

facts.statement: Stenopelix lived during the Berriasian stage, from 139.1 to 137.05 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Berriasian (139.1 to 137.05 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The preserved rump and tail combined measure 97 centimeters in length, while the femur is 14 centimeters long.
rejected.quote: The preserved rump and tail have a combined length of just 97 centimetres; the femur is fourteen centimetres long.
